_editing: Everything on the Visit page except hours and address, which come from site.json. The first-visit guide is written for someone who has never been inside a mandir — keep that reader in mind when editing.

intro.en: You are welcome exactly as you are. You do not need to be Hindu, to know Marathi, to know any of the prayers, or to have been to a mandir before. Nothing will be asked of you and nothing is expected. What follows is only so you know what to expect.
intro.mr: आपले स्वागत आहे. कोणतीही पूर्वतयारी आवश्यक नाही.

body.en: There are shelves just inside the door. Socks are perfectly fine to keep on.
Walk up to the sanctum, stand for as long as you like, and fold your hands if that feels natural. Many devotees bow; you are not required to. There is no queue on ordinary days.
A slow clockwise circuit around the sanctum. Any number is fine; many do it once, some do eleven.
Floor seating with cushions, and chairs along the side wall for anyone who needs them. Sit for two minutes or two hours.
Offered with the right hand and received with both. It is food that has been offered first — eating it is part of the visit, not an obligation.

etiquette.en: Dress is informal. Modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is appreciated.
Photography is fine in the hall, but please not during aarti.
Please silence phones inside the sanctum.
Offerings of flowers, fruit or a coconut are welcome, and entirely optional.
Children are genuinely welcome — noise is not a problem here.

offering.en: If you would like to make an offering, flowers, fruit, a coconut or dry sweets are all traditional. Please do not bring anything containing meat, eggs, onion or garlic into the sanctum.
offering.mr: फुले, फळे, नारळ किंवा सुका खाऊ अर्पण करता येतो.

summary.en: Free parking is available in the lot at 2350 Paragon Dr. On ordinary darshan days there is ample space.
summary.mr: २३५० Paragon Dr येथे मोफत वाहनतळ उपलब्ध आहे.

notes.en: On utsav days the lot fills early — arrive at least thirty minutes before the programme, or plan to use street parking on Paragon Dr.
Accessible bays are marked nearest the entrance and are kept clear for blue-badge holders.
Volunteers direct parking on Pragat Din. Please follow their guidance rather than the usual bays.
Please do not park in neighbouring business lots — we share this block.

summary.en: The mandir is on a single level with step-free access from the parking lot to the sanctum.

features.en: Step-free entrance and a single-level interior
Accessible parking bays nearest the entrance
Chairs available for anyone who cannot sit on the floor
Seating reserved near the front for devotees with limited mobility, on request

contactNote.en: If there is something you need in order to attend comfortably, call (408) 785-1450 or email info@shrigajananseva.org before you come. We would much rather arrange it in advance.
contactNote.mr: आपल्याला काही विशेष सोयीची आवश्यकता असल्यास आधी संपर्क साधा.

q.en: Do I need to be Hindu to visit?

a.en: No. The mandir is open to anyone who wishes to come. Maharaj's central teaching was that no being is separate from God — that includes you, whatever you believe.

q.en: Is there an entry fee or a donation expectation?

a.en: No, to both. There is a donation box, and nobody watches it.
Yes, and please do. Children are welcome in every part of the mandir and noise is not a problem.

q.en: I don't read Marathi. Can I still follow the upasana?

a.en: Yes. The Upasana Booklet includes transliteration, and you are welcome to simply sit and listen. Many regular devotees followed along for months before they joined in.

q.en: Can I offer Shrungar Seva or sponsor a mahaprasad?

a.en: Yes. Both are arranged in advance — speak to a trustee on a darshan day or email info@shrigajananseva.org.

q.en: Is the mandir open on days other than Thursday, Saturday and Sunday?

a.en: Not for general darshan. Daily seva continues online on Zoom every day of the year.
